RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for  ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday,  the April 17, 2008/Chaitra 28, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Coal; Communications and
Information Technology; Development of North Eastern Region;
Environment and Forests; External Affairs; Housing and Urban
Poverty Alleviation; Overseas Indian Affairs; Panchayati Raj;
ParliamentaryAffairs; Personnel, Public Grievances and
Pensions; Planning; Shipping, Road Transport and
Highways; Space; Statistics and Programme
Implementation; Urban Development;
Y outh Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions — 20
Underground fire in Jharia Coalfield
area
*361. SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that around seven
lakh people in Jharia Coalfield area in
Jharkhand are affected due to underground
fire; and
(b) if so, the steps taken by Government
to protect the lives and livelihood of the
people affected, environment and the areas
by controlling the underground fire?
Reduction in remuneration of people
working in IT industries
†*362. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is an
indication of further reduction in the
remuneration of the people working in
Information and Technology Industries of
the country;
(b) if so, whether it is a fact that there
would be an annual increase of 10 to 12 per
cent in the remuneration of people working
in these industries in comparison to 16 to
20 per cent increase during the past years;
(c) if so, the facts thereof; and
(d) whether the main reason of this
reduction is continous recession in the
American economy?
Special Purpose Vehicle for coal
*363. SHRI JESUDASU SEELAM:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government gave its
approval to the Special Purpose Vehicle
(SPV) formed by the steel companies to
acquire coal properties abroad to meet their
needs;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
114

115
(b) whether the proposed SPV would
have an authorised capital base of rupees
ten thousand crore and a paid-up capital of
rupees three thousand five hundred crore;
(c) whether Steel Authority of India
Limited, Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited,
Coal India Limited, National Mineral
Development Corporation and NTPC have
joined hands to acquire coal properties
abroad, especially in Australia and Canada;
and
(d) if so, to what extent it would be
helpful in overcoming the coal shortage in
the country?
E-auction of coalfields
†*364. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY: Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
e-auction has led to a conflict-like situation
in Chhendipara open cast project (OCP)
under Orissa-based Mahanadi Coalfields
Ltd. (MCL) over the past few months;
(b) whether that OCP is closed for
months together;
(c) whether this has led to
discontentment among local populace, who
have taken to agitation; and
(d) if so, the measures Government has
taken to address this problem?
Funds for sports at school/college
level
*365. SHRI SU. THIRUNA VUK-
KARASAR: Will the Minister of YOUTH
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS  be pleased to
state:
(a) the amount of money allotted to
every State to develop sports or games at
school level and at college level; and
(b) whether there is any proposal to
construct stadiums  at the Block level?
Rising number of vehicles and
parking problem in cities
*366. DR. LAXMINARAY AN
SHARMA: Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the reasons of unprecedented
increase in the number of vehicles in Metro
cities;
(b) whether Government is aware that
it may result in traffic and parking
problems; and
(c) if so, the steps that are being taken
to solve the problem and restrict the
purchase of vehicles?
Y amuna Action Plan
†*367. SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ : Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Yamuna is
one of the most polluted rivers in the world;
(b) if so, whether any action plan for
Yamuna has been prepared on the lines of
Ganga Action Plan; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Allotment of flats under journalists'
quota
†*368. SHRI ALI ANW AR ANSARI:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether a policy was formulated to
fix two per cent quota for the journalists
accredited by Press Information Bureau
(PIB) for allotment of flats constructed by
the Delhi Development Authority (DDA);
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

116
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) whether it is a fact that a large
number of PIB accredited journalists are
homeless;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
Government has not invited applications
for the allotment of flats in journalists'
quota for the last several years;
(d) if so, whether Government
proposes to allot unoccupied DDA flats
to homeless journalists under the
journalists' quota; and
(e) if so, by when and if not, the reasons
therefor?
Penalty on different telecom
companies
†*369. SHRI PYARELAL
KHANDELW AL: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that penalty of
almost more than rupees eight hundred
crore has been imposed on different telecom
companies in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the names of companies alongwith
amount of penalty imposed  on them and
the reasons imposing such penalty;
(d) the amount of penalty recovered by
Government from the said companies, so
far;
(e) the details of the action being taken
by Government in this regard;
(f) the action taken so far by
Government against the guilty companies
who have not paid penalty; and
(g) by when Government would recover
the said amount?
Coal production in the country
*370. SHRI VIJAYKUMAR RUPANI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Coal
availability is less than that of production
in our country;
(b) the coal production in our country
for the last five years from 2002-03 to
2006-07 and the share of Coal India Ltd.
thereof and the demand met by CIL and
private sector;
(c) the plans to explore underground
coal gasification to be used as a fuel in view
of the "Proved" and "Indicated" deposits
having immense potential; and
(d) how much is the current level of
energy consumption in India compared to
developed and developing countries?
Recovery of dues from private
operators by BSNL
*371. SHRI HARISH RAWA T:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether BSNL has to recover
several crores from its subscribers and
private operators;
(b) if so, the facts and details thereof;
(c) whether BSNL has chalked out plans
to recover such dues from subscribers and
private operators within a time schedule;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) w hether any responsibility has
been fixed on officials of BSNL, who
have failed to recover such huge
outstanding dues; and

117
(f) if so, the details thereof?
Illegal  workers  in  foreign
countries
*372. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the  Minister of OVERSEAS INDIAN
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the estimated number of Indian
workers illegally working in the foreign
countries  especially  in  the  Gulf
countries;
(b) whether the passports and other
documents of the workers from India are
being seized by their employers;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the steps taken by Government to
render necessary assistance and protect
such workers from harassment and
deportation?
Global warming
*373. SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI : Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
if climatic trends continue unabated, global
warming would threaten our health, our
cities, our farms and forests, beaches and
wetlands and other natural habitats;
(b) if so, the impact on above segments
likely to occur in India, sector-wise;
(c) whether, recently, Government
accepted the fact of impact of global
warming on agriculture and irregular rain;
(d) if so, the details and measures taken;
and
(e) the programme Government has
launched to create awareness on global
warming?
Indians in foreign jails
*374. DR. ABHISHEK MANU
SINGHVI:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS  be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government agrees that
6277 Indian citizens are languishing in
foreign jails for travelling with false
documents as revealed during deliberations
in the recently concluded Pravasi Bhartiya
Sammelan (January, 2008); and
(b) if so, whether any efforts are on the
anvil to get them back to India especially
from  UAE, Singapore, Pakistan, Saudi
Arabia, Malaysia, etc. where their
concentration is significant?
New Forest Bill
*375. KUMARI NIRMALA
DESHPANDE: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) the States that have framed rules
and regulations to implement  the policy
after the passing of the new Forest Bill,
giving rights to the original forest dwellers;
(b) whether it is a fact that the tribals
are being harassed when they try to take
the possession of their land; and
(c) by when and in what manner the
harassment of tribals would stop?
Coal to oil project of Tatas
*376. DR. V . MAITREY AN : Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Inter
Ministerial Group (IMG) has approved a
huge project of Tatas with Sasol of South
Africa for coal to oil project;
(b) if so, the total cost of the project;

118
(c) whether there are similar projects
waiting for clearance from Government and
if so, the details thereof and the time by
which they would be approved;
(d) the estimated quantity of oil that is
going to be converted from coal and the
cost efficiency of the project; and
(e) by when this project would be
commissioned?
Misleading information under RTI Act
*377. SHRIMATI SYEDA
ANW ARA TAIMUR:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry had provided
misleading information under RTI Act
stating that the "purpose of Minister's visit
to Panama and Cairo from 4—10
November, 2004 was not known and that
the trip was not sponsored by the
Department";
(b) if so, whether it was later on, after it
had appeared in print media, explained that
he had visited Egypt and Panama in 2004
accompanied by senior officials, and held
several meetings with canal authorities and
Government; and
(c) who is responsible for providing
misleading information under RTI Act and
the action taken thereon?
Difference in Socio-economic
standards among States
†*378. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the gap in
socio-economic standards of existing 28
States of the country has become a matter
of concern;
(b) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto;
(c) whether Government has identified
the backward and developed States
separately and if so, the names thereof;
and
(d) whether any provision has been
made to implement Special Development
Scheme in backward as well as most
backward States during the Eleventh Five
Year Plan period?
Monthly remuneration for Hockey
players
*379. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS
AND SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Hockey players selected in
the National Team are entitled to monthly
remuneration;
(b) if so, the details of amount paid to
each player, separately for men and women
players;
(c) whether Government is aware of
reports of delays in payment to these
players;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the steps taken to avoid such delays?
Shortage of housing units
*380. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND
URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
there is a shortage of three crore housing
units in the country;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

119
(b) if so, the number of units
Government    proposes   to   build
during  the  Eleventh  Five  Year  Plan
period  particularly  for  the  people  of
low  and  medium  income  group  in  the
country;
(c) whether Government would provide
special incentives to private sector for this
purpose; and
(d) the number of Government
sponsored projects going on with the details
of projects, city-wise?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 10th April, 2008 Secretary-General.
Chaitra 21, 1930 (Saka)
